subject: re-doc
title: (R)RE.DOC.------C.CONT.
description: First of two diagrams in CMOA(II)-53 facing Braxton's account of the 'suppression cycle' — 'this is the period where one asks the question "whatever happened to ole Joe?" From a dynamic beginning, where a given thrust alignment served as basis for both new projectional forms and vitality, and in doing so provided the vibrational uplift for composite world culture, to a suppressed scattering of surprised musicians (who probably are still fighting each other) — this is what I mean by trans-response-shift pattern.' The crossing diagrams the structural condition under which that pattern becomes possible: (R)RE-DOC (the *reality* of redocumentation — the cycle in which a thrust alignment gets historicized) is crossed with C-CONT (composite continuance — whether the form's actual vibrational thrust keeps moving). RE-DOC sits in the lower-left with the subject-arrow, and the main line runs up-right to C-CONT, which has no branches of its own. TRS (transition) rises from the main line; SOC-RT-DY (social-reality dynamics) branches from it to the left, with PART (participation) hanging from SOC-RT-DY just above the subject, and SPT-DYM (spiritual dynamics) branches from it to the right, with ALT-F (alternative functionalism) rising from the SPT-DYM line. Lower down, INFO-F (information focus) branches from the main line to the right; AF-NT (affinity nature) drops from it to anchor the bottom-center, and AFTF (affinity transfer) rises from it, with CRTF-PROG (cross-transfer progressionalism) hanging off AFTF at the far lower-right. Structural argument: redocumentation crossed with composite-continuance builds its side structure from two points on the main line, transition above and information-focus below.
